question: A 63-year-old man, who has been receiving an antidepressant for 3 years. He comes to the emergency room due to an intense hypertensive crisis, with tachycardia and headache. The patient reports that the day before he was watching the football game in a bar, and that he has taken a sandwich of cheese and sausages, and over 3 glasses of beers. What antidepressant could it be?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Cheese and sausages -> contains tyramine -> Tranylcypromine (MAOI) interacts with tyramine -> Hypertensive crisis -> Tranylcypromine (MAOI) possible -> 70% CHAIN: Alcohol consumption -> Fluoxetine (SSRI) -> No known interaction with alcohol causing hypertensive crisis -> Unlikely to be Fluoxetine -> 80% CHAIN: Headache, tachycardia -> Possible serotonin syndrome -> Venlafaxine (SNRI) or Duloxetine (SNRI) -> Possible -> 60% CHAIN: Hypertensive crisis, tachycardia -> Possible anticholinergic effects -> Imipramine (TCA) -> Possible -> 70%
